distinguishing_features: A PCB/component lead-frame configuration with four solder pads/joints contacted in parallel instead of two.
Spatial division of dissipated heat among multiple solder-joint paths to lower heat flux and local ΔT per joint.
Use of Coffin-Manson per-joint thermal excursion as the solder-interconnect fatigue-life criterion.
A fabricated PCB comparison measuring solder-joint-center ΔT rather than turbine telemetry-based inference and derating.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce cyclic thermo-mechanical fatigue damage in PCB solder interconnects caused by CTE mismatch during power cycling.
parsed.viable_reason: Adding parallel solder joints may divide heat flow through those paths, but it does not reduce the imposed CTE-mismatch excursion/relative displacement under the stated cycling, and the external thermal-cycling test fixes the same ΔT for both boards so the claimed 75% drop is not attainable as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Providing additional parallel solder pads/lead-frame contacts and copper spreading to share heat and reduce per-joint load is a routine PCB/package design measure, so the distinguishing mechanism would be obvious.
